overview:
Josh Gottheimer, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a northern New Jersey district that leans two points toward Democrats. He enters the general election with an enormous financial advantage: more than $12.7 million in cash on hand, against roughly $9,000 for Republican Sean Kirrane, who has raised under $100,000. No outside spending for or against either candidate has been reported, and a minor independent candidate is also on the ballot.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket each price the Democratic nominee around 96 percent to win. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on the district's lean, the incumbency advantage, and the fundraising gap. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty lying in the size of the winning margin rather than the outcome itself.
